title: Fireteam Zero - A Weird War 2 game - Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NWOjsRjPomI

Daniel (@dungeondive) reviews Fireteam Zero, a Weird War II tactical squad game he pitches as radically stripped-down. Where "fast-paced" crawlers like Zombicide bog down in setup and fiddling, this one puts everything you need on the table at once — never more than five enemy minis, cycling through a spawn pool rather than constantly digging through the box. Heroes are a deck of cards and a miniature: each card doubles as an attack (matching values combine into bigger dice pools), a reaction, and your health — spend cards to hit and you're left defenceless next turn. The map plays more like area control than a dungeon crawl, with monsters spawning at tokens and a threat track that periodically deals a "twist" card that cranks enemy power (one made every attack deal a minimum of two damage). A ten-page rulebook gets you playing in half an hour, and Daniel lost the opening scenario twice inside 30 minutes without resentment — it's that quick to reset. His verdict: don't expect the epic sprawl of Perdition's Mouth or a Flying Frog box; expect a lean, repeatable skirmish game that earns its table time through sheer speed.

----

Do you value a game that hits the table in 30 minutes over one that dazzles with variety — or does a lean skirmish like Fireteam Zero run dry too fast for you?
